title: Syria Destroys First Assad-Era Chemical Munitions Since 2014, OPCW Tells UN Security Council
detail: The Organisation for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons confirmed that Syrian authorities, under OPCW supervision, irreversibly destroyed 42 aerial bombs from the former Assad government's undeclared chemical weapons program — the first verified chemical munitions destruction in Syria since 2014. OPCW Director-General briefed the UN Security Council on September 3, 2026, calling it 'significant progress' following the transitional government's May 2026 discovery of undeclared chemical materials, a June amended declaration identifying storage sites at Al-Qutayfah and Homs plus a nerve-agent precursor facility, and the OPCW Executive Council's July 2026 restoration of Syria's rights under the Chemical Weapons Convention. Inspectors verified during an August 2026 deployment that remaining inventories matched Syria's declarations.

media.caption: Syria begins destroying remnants of the Assad-era chemical weapons program under OPCW supervision
